title: Prefill probe: attention-prefetcher that routes INT8/FP8 paths based on early-token signals
text:
Prefill probe: attention-prefetcher that routes INT8/FP8 paths based on early-token signals

description:
Problem: Dequantization overhead and poor kernel choice during prefill can add 10-40% tail latency for streaming workloads. Goal: implement a lightweight "prefill probe" that examines the first N tokens and microbatch characteristics to pick an execution path (pure INT8 fastpath, FP8 fallback, or mixed-precision hybrid) and decide whether to delay dequant into a short-lived slab to amortize casting costs across tokens that will hit the KV cache.

Scope: prototype probing heuristics, an attention-prefetcher module in the runtime scheduler, a small telemetry surface, and an A/B test on hosted API routing. This ticket contains the design, implementation tasks, perf benchmarks, and rollout plan for the probe and short-lived dequant slab mechanism.

acceptance_criteria:
Probe adds <0.5ms median overhead to prefill for 1-8 token prompts
End-to-end tail latency reduction >=10% on representative streaming workloads (dialogue, code-completion) vs baseline INT8-first route with immediate dequant
No increase in token error rate (measured via baseline eval set) beyond 0.5% for generation quality metrics
Circuit-breaker that disables probe when memory contention increases beyond threshold
Server-side telemetry emitted (probe decisions + chosen kernel path + KV-reuse ratio) and dashboards linked
Automated canary rollout with rollback if p50 latency regresses >5% or error rate >1%

design_notes:
Probe window: first 2 tokens of prefill + microbatch size and sequence length distribution from recent requests (10s sliding window)
Heuristic scoring: compute quick features (token entropy proxy, average head sparsity estimate, microbatch weight) -> score maps to path: INT8-fast, mixed, FP8-safe
Short-lived dequant slab: allocate ephemeral buffer for dequantized activations and mark for reuse for K steps; free after fallback or after hit-rate falls below 30%
Kernel selection: add light-weight policy hook in kernel arbiter so probe output becomes a hint, not a hard binding; allows graceful fallback to baseline kernels if kernel reservation fails
Safety: fall back to FP8 when probe confidence < 0.6 or when memory pressure is high; add global rate limit for probe-enabled requests to avoid stress during bursts

implementation_steps:
1) Runtime: add PrefillProbe interface and integrate into prefill scheduler (Rajat)
2) Scheduler: implement ephemeral dequant slab allocator and reuse bookkeeping (Priya Shah)
3) Kernel arbiter: add hint API for kernel selection and soft-priority lane (Diego Chen)
4) Telemetry: emit probe_decision, chosen_kernel, kv_reuse_ratio, probe_latency (SRE metrics + trace tags) (Lucia)
5) Tests: microbench harness for single-GPU and multi-GPU prefill latency, regression eval on eval-suite (Ava)
6) PRs & code review: create 3 PRs (runtime, scheduler, telemetry) and coordinate cross-review
7) Canary: rollout plan on staging -> 5% production -> 25% -> 100% with rollback gates

risk_tradeoffs:
Probe complexity vs runtime overhead: simple heuristics preferred to ML model to maintain predictability; risk that heuristics misclassify rare patterns
Memory tradeoff: ephemeral slab increases peak memory; capped to 10% of model activation budget per worker and evicted under pressure
Quality vs cost: INT8 fastpath lowers cost but can degrade generation quality for some prompts. We will maintain quality thresholds and allow model-specific overrides
Operational complexity: additional telemetry and gating introduces more knobs; rollouts must be gradual and observability must be in place before wide rollout

benchmarks:
Baseline: immediate dequant + INT8 attempt: p99 prefill latency 38.2ms on c5g.xlarge-like test harness
Probe + short-lived slab (canary): p99 prefill latency 31.6ms (17% improvement) on dialogue workload; median overhead of probe 0.42ms
FP8 fallback path measured separately: quality diff (BLEU/ROUGE proxy) <0.3% on eval set
KV reuse: slab amortizes dequant work for 62% of requests with >3 tokens reused within 5 steps

telemetry_and_dashboards:
Metrics to emit: probe_latency_ms, probe_confidence, chosen_path (INT8|MIXED|FP8), dequant_slab_hit, slab_eviction_count
Dashboard: /dashboards/runtime/quant-prefill-probe (staging link) https://internal.redwood/dashboards/runtime/quant-prefill-probe
Alerting: p50/p99 latency regression alerts, error-rate elevated open rate, slab memory eviction spike >10/min

comments:
2026-01-20 - Ava Martinez: Initial design sketched during runtime sync. Decided to prefer heuristics over an ML probe for predictability.
2026-02-02 - Rajat Kapoor: Implemented PrefillProbe interface skeleton and unit tests. Local single-GPU perf looks promising (0.4ms added overhead).
2026-02-18 - Priya Shah: Short-lived slab allocator added; need a memcap to avoid OOM on 32GB instances. Will cap per-worker slab to 8% of activation budget.
2026-02-25 - Diego Chen: Kernel arbiter hint API ready, but we need a fallback path for kernels that don't accept INT8 input shapes. Filed TODO to add shape-to-kernel mapping table.
2026-03-03 - Lucia (SRE): Telemetry wire format reviewed; added span tags for probe_confidence. Instrumentation PR open: observability#829.
2026-03-08 - QA: Staging A/B run (5k requests) shows 12% p99 reduction on code-completion corpus, but one outlier prompt triggered repeated slab evictions — adding evictionbackoff.
2026-03-11 - PM Review (J. Patel): Approve canary rollout. Ensure runbooks updated and add rollback playbook to incident docs.
2026-03-12 - Rajat Kapoor: Canary rollout scheduled for 2026-03-16 at 10:00 UTC to 5% traffic. Monitoring dashboards linked above.
